description: Robert Ferringo review, checked 7 Nov 2026: Doc's Sports package prices, the credit guarantee, his record claims and what a buyer can verify.
dek: A longtime Doc's Sports writer and handicapper who sells picks in six sports through the Doc's store, from $25 a day to $850 a season. His sales page is packed with winning runs and season counts, but no full pick log, and several of the numbers do not match each other.

short_answer: Robert Ferringo is a real, named handicapper who writes weekly articles for Doc's Sports and sells picks through the Doc's store, which publishes its prices and names its operator. In that narrow sense the service is legitimate.

Whether his picks make money is not answered by anything we could open. His Doc's page lists dozens of runs, such as "100-57, +29,600" on 8 unit plays and "+65,080 NOV-DEC PROFIT" in college basketball, all chosen and graded by the seller. Some of those figures change from one Doc's page to the next.

He describes himself as a volume handicapper who may send many plays a day, so a buyer is paying for a lot of action, not a few picks. If you buy, buy short, log every pick with the line and time you received it, and judge it after a few hundred plays.

guarantee: Ferringo's packages use the standard Doc's Sports guarantee. On packages of a week or longer, the page says that if the package "finishes at a loss, you can extend your service for free through our self-extend program." One day packages get an account credit the next morning instead, and two of them count a small profit as a failure: college basketball pays the $30 credit unless the day makes at least $40, and NHL unless it makes at least $35.

We found no cash refund terms on any page we opened. A losing buyer gets more Ferringo picks or store credit at Doc's. Losses on the bets themselves are never covered. Because he releases many plays, those bet losses can be much larger than the package price.

claims_note: Several numbers do not agree with each other. His page says "14 OF 20" winning college basketball years in two places, while the bio on the same page says 15 of 20. The same "+15,180" college basketball run is dated to 2025 in the header and to 2024 lower down. His page puts 2023 to 2025 college basketball profit at +21,520, while the season special page says +20,700 and gives a 5.0 and up record of 599-398 where his page says 588-392. None of these figures is backed by a log we could open.

The bankroll claim cannot be checked: the current page does not say what date "now" means. The dollar figures are presumably at $100 a unit, as his 2014 article states, but the current page does not say so, and it shows neither the prices taken nor the losing stretches around each run.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: nothing that covers his full history. We found no full, time stamped log of every Ferringo pick with the line, the price and the post time, no third party monitor record, and no contest results run by an outside organizer. Our searches found no court or regulator action involving him.

What is the seller's own marketing: every record on his page is a run, a subset or a count of winning seasons chosen and graded by Doc's Sports. The Doc's FAQ says it grades with "the line that is the general consensus at the time of posting", which may not be the line a buyer actually gets. Counts such as "11 OF 17 WINNING FB YRS" leave out how much the losing years lost.

In his own 2014 article he calls himself "a volume handicapper" who will release 26 college basketball plays on a Saturday. A high volume record can be judged fairly only from the full log, because the selected runs on the page are a small part of what he sends.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition Robert Ferringo is not matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how his picks perform.
our_data.context: For scale: his page highlights records near 60%, such as 588-392 on college basketball plays rated 5.0 and up. On the Watchdog board on 7 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: We found almost no independent customer evidence about Robert Ferringo himself. His Doc's page carries no testimonials, and the forum discussion we found is about Doc's Sports in general. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: In a TheRX thread about Doc's Sports, a member who said he tracks the Doc's handicappers daily wrote that they highlight hot runs and never mention cold streaks, and named the house handicapper and Raphael Esparza as the worst. He did not name Ferringo and did not post a log. We did not verify his figures.
The same thread was opened by a bettor who said he had used Doc's Sports off and on for more than 10 years and asked for feedback. Nobody in the thread discussed Ferringo's picks.

Our searches found no Reddit, Covers or SportsbookReview thread with a real discussion of Ferringo's picks, and no Trustpilot or Better Business Bureau profile for him as an individual. Evidence is too thin to say what a typical buyer experiences.

conflicts: Ferringo sells only through Doc's Sports, so the Doc's conflicts apply. The Doc's FAQ says: "We have a list of offshore sports book that we have complete confidence in." On 7 Nov 2026 a free pick on the Doc's homepage listed the line as "Offered at: BookMaker", and that link redirected through a revenue share tracking address to a BookMaker promotion page. Revenue share deals usually pay the referrer a cut of what referred customers lose.

Offshore sportsbooks are not licensed by U.S. state regulators. Check the law where you live before you follow that advice. He also writes free articles for Doc's, such as weekly NFL power rankings, which promote the same store.
strengths: A named handicapper with a long public writing history at Doc's, including weekly articles in 2026.
Prices and guarantee terms are written out per package on his page, so a buyer sees the rules before paying.
He states his approach openly: many plays, unit ratings, and a long term view, so buyers know what kind of service to expect.
concerns: No full public record. Every number on his page is a run, a subset or a season count chosen by the seller.
Several of his advertised figures conflict with each other across Doc's pages.
The guarantee replaces a losing package with more picks or credit. It never returns money and never covers betting losses.
The Doc's FAQ points readers to offshore sportsbooks, and the site carries a sportsbook revenue share link.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: He is a real handicapper and longtime Doc's Sports writer who sells picks through a store with published prices and a named operator. We could not verify that his picks win over time, because no full record of every pick is published.
How much does Robert Ferringo cost?

On 7 Nov 2026 his Doc's page sold one day packages for $25 to $30, weekly packages for $89 to $99, monthly packages for $279 to $325, and season packages from $495 (rest of football season) to $850 (NBA).
Does Robert Ferringo have a verified record?

No. His page shows runs and winning season counts graded by Doc's Sports, some of which conflict with other Doc's pages, and we found no full pick log, outside monitor or contest record. Watchdog has no graded record for him.

For the money you get a high volume of picks with unit ratings in up to six sports, and a losing package is extended or credited rather than refunded. What is unproven is whether those picks, at the lines a buyer can get, beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over hundreds of plays.
